title: Permutations and Combinations: ⁿPᵣ, ⁿCᵣ and Counting
seo_title: Permutations and Combinations Class 11 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 6)
standard_text: Fundamental principle of counting; factorial n (n!); permutations and combinations, derivation of formulae for ⁿPᵣ and ⁿCᵣ and their connections; simple applications (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 11 Permutations and Combinations worksheet (NCERT Chapter 6): counting principle, factorials, ⁿPᵣ, ⁿCᵣ, arrangements of letters, digits, committees and teams. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Order matters → permutation; order does not matter → combination.
key_sub: ⁿPᵣ = n!/(n − r)!, ⁿCᵣ = n!/(r!(n − r)!).
body_html:
How it works

  • Counting principle: if one thing can be done in m ways and the next in n ways, both can be done in mn ways.
  • n! = n(n − 1)(n − 2)…1, and 0! = 1.
  • Arrangements (order matters): nPr = n! ÷ (n − r)!.
  • Selections (order does not matter): nCr = n! ÷ (r!(n − r)!), and nCr = nCn−r.
  • Repeated letters: n! ÷ (p! q! …) where a letter appears p times, another q times, and so on.
Example

How many arrangements of the letters of ALLAHABAD are there?

9 letters: A 4 times, L twice

9! ÷ (4! 2!)

Answer: 7,560

Common mistakes

  • Adding the choices instead of multiplying them.
  • Using ⁿPᵣ for a committee, where order does not matter.
  • Forgetting to divide by the factorials of repeated letters.
